sentences.text: The brief facts of the case as per claim petition are that the deceased Ajit Tomar was a contractor and on 21.04.2018 at 03:30 a.m., while he was busy in his work at the construction site at Main Road, near Village Gauri Pur, District Baghpat, U.P., all of a sudden, a Container (make-Ashok Leyland) bearing registration no. HR46E-6938, (in short 'offending vehicle'), being driven by its driver at a fast speed, rashly and negligently, came and ran over him, as a result, he died on spot.
He was taken to District Combined Hospital, Baghpat, where he was declared brought dead and his postmortem was conducted.
In connection with the accident, FIR no.594/2018, under sections 279/337/338/304-A IPC was registered at PS Baghpat.

However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of preponderance of probabilities.
Holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.

He categorically stated that the registration number of the offending vehicle was HR46E- 6938 and he had noted down the said registration number on his palm.

sentences.text: After going through his entire evidence, it is comprehensible that he was present at the spot at the time of accident and thus, his admission that "it is correct that I was not present at the time of accident" appears to have been wrongly recorded.

This inference finds further support from the fact that in the very next sentence, PW2 states that "it is further wrong to suggest xxxxx", which indicates that prior to denying this suggestion, he might have denied the suggestion given as "it is wrong to suggest that I was not present at the time of accident", and instead of recording the said suggestion so, it was wrongly recorded in the evidence that "it is correct that I was not present at the time of accident".
12.

Also, I may note that PW2 categorically stated thereafter that driver of the offending vehicle was apprehended by the public and gave clear picture of the spot by stating that the the road was broken,
that the truck came at a high speed and that the truck was of six tyres and that the width of the road was about 22 feet.

In the circumstances, it is abundantly evident that PW2 had witnessed the accident and that is why he had been able enough to describe the relevant facts as well as details of occurrence of accident categorically.

sentences.text: It will also be easier for the insurance companies to settle accident claims without delay.

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
S t e p - 2 ( A s c e r t a i n i n g t h e m u l t i p l i e r )

sentences.text: Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
Having regard to several imponderables in life and economic factors, a table of multipliers with reference to the age has been identified by this Court.
The multiplier should be chosen from the said table with reference to the age of the deceased.
Step-3 (Actual Calculation)

The annual contribution to the family (multiplicand)
when multiplied by such multiplier gives the 'loss of dependency' to the family.
Thereafter, a conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000/- to Rs.10,000/- may be added as loss of estates.
Where the deceased is survived by his widow, another conventional amount in the range of Rs.5,000 to Rs.10,000 should be added under the head of loss of consortium.
But no amount is to be awarded under the head of pain, suffering or hardship caused to the legal heirs of the deceased.

PW1 Devender Tomar deposed that his son Ajit Tomar (deceased) was working as Civil Contractor as well as Agriculturist and was earning Rs.50,000/- per month,
however, he did not place on record any document to show the occupation or income of the deceased.
As per academic documents Ex.PW1/E to Ex.PW1/H, the deceased had passed intermediate examination.
Further, the aadhaar card of petitioners and that of deceased clearly show their residential address of Delhi.

In the circumstances,
in absence of any documentary evidence in support of income of deceased, his income has to be assessed at par with minimum wages applicable to matriculate category of workers prevalent in Delhi on the date of accident (21.04.2018), which were Rs.16,858/- per month.
Thus, the income of the deceased is considered to be Rs.16,858/- per month.

sentences.text: After choosing the age, multiplier and income of the deceased, necessary deductions have to be made out of the income of the deceased towards his personal expenses.

The deceased was 25 years of age and was unmarried at the time of accident because as per averments made in the petition there were only three dependents i.e. parents and younger brother of the deceased.

With respect to deductions towards personal living expenses of a bachelor, the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Pranay Sethi & Others (Supra) laid down the guiding principle as under:
"31.
Where the deceased was a bachelor and the claimants are the parents, the deduction follows a different principle.
In regard to bachelors, normally 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.

Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event the contribution to the parent(s)
and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.

Further, subject to evidence to the contrary,
the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependent and the mother alone will be considered as a dependent.

In the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents, because they will either be independent and earning, or married, or be dependent on the father."
Therefore, in this case, 50% of the income of the deceased has to be deducted towards his personal living expenses.

These issues to be determined by the Tribunal to arrive at the loss of dependency are:

19. To have uniformity and consistency, the Tribunals should determine compensation in cases of death, by the following well-settled steps:
Step-1 (Ascertaining the multiplicand)
The income of the deceased per annum should be determined.
Out of the said income a deduction should be made in regard to the amount which the deceased would have spent on himself by way of personal and living expenses.
The balance which is considered to be the contribution to the dependent family, constitutes the multiplicand.
Having regard to the age of the deceased and period of active career, the appropriate multiplier should be selected.
This does not mean ascertaining the number of years he would have lived or worked but for the accident.
